definitions.explanation: A deciduous tree of the genus Morus, whose leaves are the sole food of silkworms. Historically central to Japan's silk industry, and the source of edible mulberry fruit (berries) and mulberry-bark paper.

examples.english: There is a large mulberry tree in my grandmother's garden.

examples.japanese: ⟦{昔|むかし}→昔：01515_mukashi⟧、⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{地域|ちいき}→地域：01461_chiiki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{養蚕|ようさん}→養蚕：27720_yousan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{広|ひろ}く→広い：00704_hiroi⟧{桑|くわ}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{栽培|さいばい}→栽培：13108_saibai⟧⟦されていた→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: In the past, mulberry was widely cultivated in this region for silkworm raising.

notes:
A tree species historically of enormous economic importance in Japan because its leaves are the only food that silkworms (⟦{蚕|かいこ}→蚕：21218_kaiko⟧) will eat. In premodern and modern Japan up through the mid-twentieth century, entire regions were dedicated to {桑畑|くわばたけ} ('mulberry fields') to support the silk industry.

USAGE:
- The kanji {桑|くわ} is written with a distinctive three-{又|また} component on top representing leaves.
- {桑|くわ} can refer to both the tree itself and, by extension, its leaves and fruit in context.
- The edible berries are usually called {桑|くわ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{実|み}→実：03741_mi⟧ ('mulberry fruit') to distinguish from the tree.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {桑|くわ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{木|き}→木：00524_ki⟧: mulberry tree
- {桑|くわ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{葉|は}→葉：02241_ha⟧: mulberry leaf (eaten by silkworms; also used for tea)
- {桑|くわ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{実|み}→実：03741_mi⟧: mulberry berry; mulberry fruit
- {桑畑|くわばたけ}: mulberry field; mulberry orchard
- {桑|くわ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{栽培|さいばい}する→栽培する：09860_saibaisuru⟧: to cultivate mulberry

CULTURAL NOTE:
- The phrase {桑原桑原|くわばらくわばら} is a traditional incantation muttered to ward off lightning or misfortune, based on the folk belief that lightning would not strike mulberry groves.
- {桑|くわ} has its own symbol (Y) on older Japanese topographic maps to indicate mulberry fields, reflecting how common they once were.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{蚕|かいこ}→蚕：21218_kaiko⟧: silkworm — the creature that feeds on mulberry leaves.
- ⟦{養蚕|ようさん}→養蚕：27720_yousan⟧: silkworm raising; sericulture — the traditional industry supported by mulberry cultivation.
- マルベリー: mulberry — English loanword, used mainly in modern food/supplement marketing (e.g., mulberry tea).
